units.sourceHTML: The format for running the diff command is:

units.text: In the simplest case, two file names ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are given, and ⟦2⟧ compares the contents of ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧. A file name of ⟦5⟧ stands for the standard input.
units.sourceHTML: In the simplest case, two file names from-file and to-file are given, and diff compares the contents of from-file and to-file. A file name of - stands for the standard input.

units.text: If one file is a directory and the other is not, ⟦0⟧ compares the file in the directory whose name is that of the non-directory. The non-directory file must not be ⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: If one file is a directory and the other is not, diff compares the file in the directory whose name is that of the non-directory. The non-directory file must not be -.

units.text: If two file names are given and both are directories, ⟦0⟧ compares corresponding files in both directories, in alphabetical order; this comparison is not recursive unless the ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧) option is given. ⟦3⟧ never compares the actual contents of a directory as if it were a file. The file that is fully specified may not be standard input, because standard input is nameless and the notion of “file with the same name” does not apply.
units.sourceHTML: If two file names are given and both are directories, diff compares corresponding files in both directories, in alphabetical order; this comparison is not recursive unless the --recursive (-r) option is given. diff never compares the actual contents of a directory as if it were a file. The file that is fully specified may not be standard input, because standard input is nameless and the notion of “file with the same name” does not apply.

units.text: If the ⟦0⟧ option is given, the number of file names is arbitrary, and ⟦1⟧ is compared to each named file. Similarly, if the ⟦2⟧ option is given, each named file is compared to ⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: If the --from-file=file option is given, the number of file names is arbitrary, and file is compared to each named file. Similarly, if the --to-file=file option is given, each named file is compared to file.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ options begin with ‘⟦1⟧’, so normally file names may not begin with ‘⟦2⟧’. However, ⟦3⟧ as an argument by itself treats the remaining arguments as file names even if they begin with ‘⟦4⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: diff options begin with ‘-’, so normally file names may not begin with ‘-’. However, -- as an argument by itself treats the remaining arguments as file names even if they begin with ‘-’.

units.text: An exit status of 0 means no differences were found, 1 means some differences were found, and 2 means trouble.
units.sourceHTML: An exit status of 0 means no differences were found, 1 means some differences were found, and 2 means trouble.
